drivingQuestion: According to R' Yehuda, is intentionally brought-in blood disqualified only after sprinkling, or on entry?
outcomeNote: question is answered in the following unit by R' Yirmeya

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳. הָא מֵזִיד – פָּסוּל; בְּשֶׁכִּיפֵּר אוֹ בְּשֶׁלֹּא כִּיפֵּר?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» If the priest took the blood into the Sanctuary unwittingly, the blood remains fit for presentation. The Gemara infers: «But» if his taking of the blood into the Sanctuary was «intentional,» it is «disqualified.» The Gemara analyzes this halakha: Is the blood disqualified only «in» a case «where» he took the blood into the Sanctuary and «atoned,» by sprinkling it inside the Sanctuary, as claimed by Rabbi Eliezer in the mishna; «or» even «in» a case «where» he took the blood in and «did not» yet «atone,» in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon?

moves.about: from 'unwittingly fit' it follows that intentional entry disqualifies
